_comment: Floorplan + port-selection recipe for layout/bin/compose-whole.py (issue #172):
the whole-block composition of the verified sampler_core analog macro and the
verified trng_digital macro. Every number in this file is an INPUT to the
composition and is re-audited by compose-whole.py against the imported
geometry (DEF/GDS pins for the digital macro, a flat connectivity
extraction of the analog GDS for the analog macro) -- nothing here is
taken from the signal-only routed Verilog.
Frame. Micrometres, composed-cell frame. Both macros are placed with
orientation mirror_x (klt gen-compose: (x, y) -> (-x, y) about the block's
own local origin, THEN translated by origin_um). So a macro-local point
(x, y) lands at (origin.x - x, origin.y + y).
Why mirror_x on BOTH macros. trng_digital's signal pins sit on its WEST
edge (x = 0.4 um, met3, 82 pins) and SOUTH edge (y = 0.242 um, met2, 29
pins); the four raw/clock/reset pins the analog macro must reach are all on
the west edge. Mirroring puts them on the EAST edge, facing a free corridor
east of the digital macro that is wide enough for four routing lanes. The
analog macro is mirrored too because that is the orientation in which the
four digital-bound analog taps (raw_bit, raw_valid, clk, rst_n) come out in
DESCENDING x order while the four digital pins come out in ASCENDING y
order: pins ascending-y <-> taps descending-x is exactly the non-crossing
(nested-L) matching, so all four nets route on ONE layer with no crossing
(an un-mirrored analog macro would interleave raw_bit/raw_valid and force a
second routing layer). The analog macro's sampler bank (raw_bit/raw_valid/
clk/rst_n taps, y ~ -1.7 .. 5.0 local) therefore faces SOUTH, towards the
digital macro, and its ring array (en/vddr, y ~ 25 .. 30 local) is nearer
the north (pin) side.
Routing layer. klt gen-compose's sky130 routing roles stop at metal3 (met2)
except for 'top_metal' (met5, 72/20), which is the only role above met2 that
can be a routing.layer_role. met2 over the analog macro is occupied by its own
lanes, met3/met4 are not routing roles, so every inter-block / boundary /
supply route is drawn on met5 at 1.6 um (met5.width.1 floor) with the tool's
own via ladder (met2/met3/met4 landing pads + via2/via3/via4) at each port.
met5 spacing is 1.6 um, so every vertical met5 lane is at least 7 um from its
neighbours (see the x-list below). The absence of met3/met4 routing roles for
sky130 is a tool gap -- see layout/trng_whole/README.md 'Friction filed'.
Analog ports. sampler_core.gds carries NO top-level pin shapes or labels (its
compose.response.json reports ports: [], and its only top-cell label is the
internal 'vdd_link'), so each boundary connection is a hand-declared port on
existing conductor, chosen by a flat connectivity extraction of the analog GDS
(met2 unless noted). Each is audited by compose-whole.py: the port point must
lie on drawn conductor on the declared layer and the extracted net there must
carry the expected label (en1.., vddr1.., vdd, vss, clk, rst_n) or, for the six
sampler q taps (all six q nets carry the identical label set), lie inside the
right sampler_dff instance x-span of layout/sampler_core/cell.json's 'place'
stage with design/trng_top.spice's instance order (xsb->raw_bit, xsv->raw_valid,
xsr1..4->ring_bit1..4).
en1-en4      li1 pad of each ring NAND's enable gate (the only conductor on
that net), centre x = ring pitch 55.3 um multiples + 5.875, y =
vddr1-vddr4  the ring's own met2 rail (y = 29.635, 0.17 um wide, joined to a
0.42 um stub every ring stage); x picked mid-segment, >= 8 um
from every other lane (x-list below). The four rails are
distinct extracted nets and stay distinct in the composition.
vdd          the 'vdd' met2 lane at y = 31.135 (x 158..212.8).
vss          the 'vss' met2 lane at y = 34.435 (x 68.7..202.4).
q taps       the 0.42 um square met2 pad each sampler_dff's q ends on (y =
2.71), local x = instance origin + 44.9 (sb 0, sv 55.66, sr1
clk          the met2 clk lane (y = -1.7, 0.17 um wide, x 0.3..327.5).
rst_n        the met2 rst_n haul lane (y = 5.0, x 27.1..305.2).
Lane-pitch rule. Every analog port's met5 lane runs vertically, so all 18
local x values must be >= 7 um apart (met5: 1.6 um wide, 1.6 um spacing, 3 um
pads). Sorted local x: 5.875 en1, 15 vddr1, 44.9 raw_bit, 61.175 en2, 70 vddr2,
ring_bit1, 171.775 en4, 180 vddr4, 190 vdd, 211.88 ring_bit2, 267.54 ring_bit3,
323.2 ring_bit4 -- minimum gap 7.4 um (checked by layout/test_compose_whole.py).
vss and vdd are both west of every inter-macro tap in the composed frame (local
x > 124 = mirrored x < 204.77), so their gap-strip runs never cross the four
inter-macro lanes.
Digital ports. Signal pins come from trng_digital.def PINS (units 1000/um,
cross-checked against the GDS pin labels). The two supply ports are on the
DEF's met5 stripes (VPWR / VGND are SPECIAL pins with nine/eight met5
rectangles). VGND is tapped on its topmost stripe (y = 236.64, nothing above
it but the macro edge); VPWR's topmost stripe (y = 223.04) is overlaid by the
VGND stripe above it on the same layer, so it escapes WEST through its tip
(local x 239.66 -> mirrored x = origin.x - 239.66) via an escape lane OUTSIDE the
macro bbox (compose-gen's own-block guard rejects a vertical run inside the
bbox).
Boundary pads. The 16 external analog/shared pins (clk, rst_n, en1-4, vddr1-4,
ring_bit1-4, vdd, vss) terminate on 3 um square met5 pads drawn by `klt draw`
into layout/trng_whole/trng_whole_pins.gds at y = pad_row, one per analog lane,
vertically above its lane. These are the whole-block external pin shapes;
the 107 digital external signal pins are promoted label-only (pins[]) on
the digital macro's own pin shapes.
Requirement mapping. Distinct vddr1..vddr4 routes + common vdd/vss between
macros and pads = the layout obligation of DR-0003 section 8 / DR-0009's
'shared supply impedance' row (distribution geometry exists). Coupling,
period-scatter and every other measurement obligation remain open for #174.
